title: Circular 33: Works Not Protected by Copyright
supports: Opened with WebFetch and read with pdftotext. Revised 03/2021. A mere listing of ingredients or simple set of directions is uncopyrightable; a recipe that creatively explains or depicts how or why may be; registration covers text and photos, not the ingredient list, process or dish; Pie in the Sky and caesar dressing examples.

title: What Does Copyright Protect? (FAQ)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Ingredient lists not protected; substantial literary expression or a compilation such as a cookbook may be; do not register secret ingredients because applications are public; ideas, methods, names and titles not protected by copyright.

title: How copyright protects your work
supports: Opened with WebFetch. UK copyright covers original literary and artistic works including photography; protection is automatic with no application or fee; there is no register of copyright works in the UK.

title: Metric Kitchen: Cooking Measurement Equivalencies
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Approximate equivalents: 1 tsp 5 mL, 1 tbsp 15 mL, 1 fl oz 30 mL, 1 cup 240 mL, 1 pint 480 mL, 1 quart 950 mL, 1 oz 28 g, 1 lb 454 g; updated 29 Apr 2026.

title: Metric Kitchen: Culinary Measurement Tips
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Weigh rather than scoop; wrong cup type is a common error; read liquids at eye level; density matters (points to NIST SP 430); check a thermometer in boiling water; high altitude, canning and candy need adjustments; updated 29 Apr 2026.

title: Metric Kitchen: Culinary Temperature
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Approximate C and F ranges for oven words (moderate 180 to 190C, 350 to 375F); ovens vary; safe minimum internal temperatures in Celsius (62.8C plus 3-minute rest for whole cuts, 71.1C ground meat and egg dishes, 73.9C poultry and leftovers); updated 29 Apr 2026.

title: Guidance for Industry: Guidelines for Determining Metric Equivalents of Household Measures
supports: Opened with WebFetch. For nutrition labelling: 1 cup = 240 mL, 1 tbsp = 15 mL, 1 tsp = 5 mL, 1 fl oz = 30 mL, 1 oz = 28 g; guidance dated October 1993, marked final.

title: Baker's Percentage
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Flour is always 100%; other ingredients as percent of flour weight; hydration; scaling by adding percentages and dividing target dough weight to get the formula conversion factor. Vendor reference page, undated.

title: Safe Food Handling
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Safe minimum internal temperatures (145F plus 3-minute rest for whole cuts, 160F ground meat and egg dishes, 165F poultry, leftovers and casseroles, fin fish 145F or opaque); fridge 40F or below; 2-hour rule (1 hour above 90F); page current as of 5 Mar 2024.

title: Safer food, better business for caterers (full pack, PDF)
supports: Opened with WebFetch and read with pdftotext. Probe check at the thickest part; time and temperature pairs from 60C for 45 minutes to 80C for 6 seconds; hot holding 63C or above; chilled 8C or below; PPDS labelling required since October 2021.

title: Allergen guidance for food businesses
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 14 allergens; PPDS label must show the name and full ingredients with allergens emphasised; free-from claims need strict controls; vegan meals may contain traces of animal allergens. Guidance updated 17 Jul 2026 (publication page).

title: Food Allergies
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Nine major food allergens including sesame; FASTER Act signed 23 Apr 2021, effective 1 Jan 2023; page current as of 3 Nov 2026.

title: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers
publisher: EUR-Lex (Publications Office of the European Union)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Annex II list of 14; Article 21 allergen emphasis; Article 30 mandatory nutrition declaration (energy, fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein, salt); Annex V point 19 exemption for small quantities supplied directly; Article 55 dates.

title: Changes to the Nutrition Facts Label
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Added sugars; vitamin D and potassium required; serving sizes updated; dual-column labels; compliance 1 Jan 2020 ($10 million or more in food sales) and 1 Jan 2021 (smaller).

title: Small Business Nutrition Labeling Exemption
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Low-volume exemption: fewer than 100 FTE employees and fewer than 100,000 units a year, annual notice; products with nutrition claims do not qualify; retailer exemptions; web notices through FDA Industry Systems from 5 Oct 2026; page current as of 5 Oct 2026.

title: Menu Labeling Requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Chains of 20 or more locations show calories on menus and boards and give written nutrition information on request; compliance 7 May 2018; page current as of 13 Dec 2023.

title: Use of the "Healthy" Claim on Food Labeling
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Final rule announced 19 Dec 2024; criteria based on food group equivalents and limits on added sugars, sodium and saturated fat, tied to the RACC; symbol not finalised; page current as of 16 Jan 2025. Effective and compliance dates not on the page.

title: Technical guidance on nutrition labelling (PDF)
publisher: Department of Health and Social Care (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch and read with pdftotext. Order energy, fat, saturates, carbohydrate, sugars, protein, salt; per 100 g or 100 ml; Annex V point 19 read as micro businesses and local by county plus neighbouring counties or 30 miles; values from analysis, calculation or established data such as CoFID. Publication page last updated 3 Mar 2017.

title: Food labelling: giving food information to consumers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Nutrition labelling compulsory on most prepacked foods since December 2016; QUID rules; applies to Great Britain; Northern Ireland follows EU rules; last updated 20 Sep 2022.

title: Great Britain nutrition and health claims (NHC) register
publisher: Department of Health and Social Care (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Only authorised claims in the GB NHC register may be used in Great Britain; applies to England, Scotland and Wales; last updated 19 May 2026.

title: Nutrition and health claims
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Regulation (EC) 1924/2006 applies since 1 Jul 2007; claims must be clear, accurate and evidence-based; misleading claims prohibited; EU Register of claims.

title: Composition of foods integrated dataset (CoFID)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. McCance and Widdowson's nutrient data on the UK food supply as one dataset; last updated 19 Mar 2021.

title: FoodData Central
publisher: US Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service
supports: Opened with WebFetch. USDA food composition database with Foundation Foods (updated April and October), SR Legacy (final 2018), FNDDS, Experimental and Branded Foods; public domain under CC0; API available.

title: Recipe (Recipe, HowTo, ItemList) structured data
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Required name and image; recommended properties including recipeIngredient, recipeInstructions, times, recipeYield, nutrition.calories (needs recipeYield), aggregateRating, video; no step numbers in recipeInstructions; ItemList for carousels.

title: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
supports: Opened with WebFetch. People-first content; first-hand experience; no preferred word count; Who, How and Why questions including disclosing AI use where readers would wonder.

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Disclose free products, payment, free meals and affiliate commissions; clearly and in the post near the recommendation, not only in a bio or footer; platform tools may not be enough.

title: Influencers' guide (summary page)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Fourth edition, page dated 23 Oct 2026; developed with the CMA; covers when content must be labelled as an ad, affiliate links and fake reviews after the DMCC Act. Summary page only; the full PDF was not read.
